title: Tools Behind a Stop, Chosen by Cre

scenes.tts: Suppose you want a mouse in which one type of neuron glows when its calcium rises. You also want to switch that same type on with light. Put the gene for green fluorescent protein behind a promoter that every cell reads, and you get a green mouse. But you need the tools in one cell type, and nowhere else. How?
scenes.visual: Six cells. One chosen cell glows, then rings blue for light. Then every cell turns green under the label of an every-cell promoter. Then the others go dark again and a how? chip appears.
scenes.narration: Suppose you want a mouse in which one type of neuron glows when its calcium rises. You also want to switch that same type on with light. Put the gene for green fluorescent protein behind a promoter that every cell reads, and you get a green mouse. But you need the tools in one cell type, and nowhere else. How?

scenes.tts: Two kinds of tool do the work. A reporter is an engineered protein that changes its light when a signal happens. G CaMP is a calcium reporter, built from green fluorescent protein. An actuator is an engineered protein that starts a signal on command. Channelrhodopsin 2 is an actuator. Blue light opens its pore, cations flow into the neuron, and at threshold the neuron fires.
scenes.caption: Two kinds of tool do the work. A reporter is an engineered protein that changes its light when a signal happens. GCaMP is a calcium reporter, built from green fluorescent protein. An actuator is an engineered protein that starts a signal on command. Channelrhodopsin-2 is an actuator. Blue light opens its pore, cations flow into the neuron, and at threshold the neuron fires.
scenes.visual: Left cell with the reporter: calcium enters and the cell lights green. Right cell with the actuator: blue light hits a closed pore, the pore opens, cations flow in, the cell fires.
scenes.narration: Two kinds of tool do the work. A reporter is an engineered protein that changes its light when a signal happens. GCaMP is a calcium reporter, built from green fluorescent protein. An actuator is an engineered protein that starts a signal on command. Channelrhodopsin-2 is an actuator. Blue light opens its pore, cations flow into the neuron, and at threshold the neuron fires.

scenes.tts: Now give each gene a stop. Put a stop signal in front of the reporter gene, between two sites called lox P. The two sites point the same way. The actuator gene gets its own stop in the same way. With the stop in place, neither gene is read.
scenes.caption: Now give each gene a stop. Put a stop signal in front of the reporter gene, between two sites called loxP. The two sites point the same way. The actuator gene gets its own stop in the same way. With the stop in place, neither gene is read.
scenes.visual: A reporter gene on a DNA line. A stop block and two loxP triangles slot in before it. The same is built for the actuator gene. Both genes are labelled silent.
scenes.narration: Now give each gene a stop. Put a stop signal in front of the reporter gene, between two sites called loxP. The two sites point the same way. The actuator gene gets its own stop in the same way. With the stop in place, neither gene is read.

scenes.tts: Cre is an enzyme from a bacterial virus. It cuts and rejoins DNA at lox P sites. When two sites point the same way, Cre removes what lies between them. The stop is cut out. Now the gene is read, in that cell and in all its descendants.

scenes.visual: Cre chips arrive at the two loxP sites of each row. The stop blocks lift out. The genes light green and are read.
scenes.narration: Cre is an enzyme from a bacterial virus. It cuts and rejoins DNA at loxP sites. When two sites point the same way, Cre removes what lies between them. The stop is cut out. Now the gene is read, in that cell and in all its descendants.

scenes.tts: So who makes Cre? Make it from a promoter that is active in one cell type. That cell type cuts out the stops, and makes both proteins. Every other cell makes no Cre. Its stops stay in place, and it makes neither protein.
scenes.visual: Two cells, both with stopped genes. Cre appears in the chosen cell only; its stops lift out and its genes light. The other cell shows a crossed-out Cre and keeps its stops.
scenes.narration: So who makes Cre? Make it from a promoter that is active in one cell type. That cell type cuts out the stops, and makes both proteins. Every other cell makes no Cre. Its stops stay in place, and it makes neither protein.

scenes.tts: To build the mouse, breed three parts together. The first is Cre, placed in a gene that only your neuron type reads. The second is a reporter behind a stop. The third is an actuator behind a stop. Only cells that make Cre remove the stops, so only they make both proteins. Keep this rule. Tools wait behind stops, and only cells that make Cre remove them.
scenes.visual: Three part chips appear, then merge into the six-cell picture. Only the chosen cell gets reporter and actuator chips and glows; the others stay dark.
scenes.narration: To build the mouse, breed three parts together. The first is Cre, placed in a gene that only your neuron type reads. The second is a reporter behind a stop.
